**Meeting**
Regular meeting, October 17, 2017, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment is Troy High's **Focus Hope** program, introduced by Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak with principal Remo Roncone presenting the students and staff involved.

The Board then commends **51 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists**. More than a million students from some 22,000 high schools entered nationwide and only 16,000 seniors are selected; semifinalists score in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT with comparable SAT scores. The packet prints the roster with phonetic guides beside most names for reading aloud — "Sanjana Anil (Sun-juhn-ah A-nil)," "Himaneesh Yerrakalva (hi-MAHN YE-ruh-KAHL-vuh)," "Zeyu Yang (Bill Yang)." Copies of the resolution go to the students at a November 15 reception. Several names recur a year later among the 54 semifinalists of the following class — James Ge, Kathleen Gu, Lyndsey Gu, Claire Hao, James Li, Spencer Liu, Shankar Prabhu, Adithya Sanjay, Muyang Wang, Angela Wang, Megan Worrel and Elise Xia.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the September 5 special meeting and workshop, the September 19 meeting, and the August 2017 Treasurer's Report.

**Treasurer's Report — August 2017**
Total check disbursements are $8,432,205.85, the General Fund group $4,771,055.94 and the General Fund (101) itself $4,583,699.91. Adding $1,137,361.53 of wire transfers, $189,355.81 of P-Card purchases and $12,128.94 of ACH debits, less $2,938.40 of prior period voids, total disbursements in period are $9,768,113.73.

**Curriculum**
The Sex Education Advisory Board for 2017/2018 is co-chaired by **Amy Buchanan**, assistant principal at Smith, and **Nicole Jenkins**; state law requires at least half the board be parents and one parent co-chair. District personnel are Buchanan, teachers Lisa Danhoff (Troy High), Karyn Wakely (Athens) and Kevin Wilson (Boulan Park), and social worker Stacey Schoenherr (Smith); clergy is Rev. Gregg Mayberry of Big Beaver United Methodist; the health resource is David Roth of the Oakland Health Department. The following year's list is nearly identical with Kristy Pierce replacing Buchanan as the district co-chair.

**Business — the 2016-2017 audit**
David Youngstrom of Yeo & Yeo presents; a draft had gone to the Board at the October workshop.

The financial statements receive an **unmodified opinion** — the highest level of assurance — that they present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the district as of June 30, 2017.

| Fund | Fund balance, June 30, 2017 |
| --- | --- |
| General Fund | $24,205,391 |
| 2016 Capital Projects | $36,718,462 |
| Nonmajor governmental | $8,368,346 |
| **Total governmental** | **$69,292,199** |

Government-wide, total assets are $85,409,988 against total liabilities of $16,117,789, with cash and investments of $64,971,528 and $18,867,458 due from other governmental units. Revenues and other sources across all governmental funds are $212,602,835 against expenditures and other uses of $183,114,138 — a **$29,488,697 change in fund balance**, of which $36,718,462 is the newly created 2016 Capital Projects Fund and the nonmajor funds fall $9,902,871.

General Fund revenue: state $97,064,534 (67%), local $38,211,378 (26%), interdistrict sources $7,610,128 (5%), federal $3,281,077 (2%) and other $60,309. Expenditures by function: instruction $99,214,158 (69%), supporting services $43,617,694 (30%), capital outlay $619,824 (1%) and other $102,644. Instructional share has held at 68–69% across three years against an Oakland County average of 63%.

Per-pupil General Fund revenue rises from $10,641 in 2013 to $11,353 in 2017, expenses from $10,585 to $11,145. Ten-year enrollment runs 12,174, 12,177, 12,076, 12,032, 12,312, 12,438, 12,591, 12,563, 12,717 and 12,881. The **General Fund unassigned balance** moves $21,433,250, $21,000,702, $20,231,419, $21,038,513 and **$23,716,299** across 2013–2017.

**The one qualification.** Internal controls show no material weaknesses and no significant deficiencies, with management comments on federal procedures and time and effort record keeping. But on major federal programs, while the Special Education Cluster receives an unmodified opinion, the **Nutrition Cluster receives a qualified opinion**, carrying a **material weakness for excess fund balance** and a **significant deficiency for student eligibility**. Federal school-meal rules cap how much surplus a food service fund may carry; the district's food service fund balance had grown past that limit.

Future challenges named: the state economic and political condition, rising fringe benefit costs, the retirement rate increase, and **eroding state revenue sources**.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, October 17, 2017, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Troy High School – Focus Hope, B. 2017-18 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda — A. Minutes of the September 5, 2017 Special Board of Education Meeting, B. Minutes of the September 5, 2017 Board of Education Workshop, C. Minutes of the September 19, 2017 Board of Education Meeting, D. Treasurer's Report – August 2017; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum — A. Consideration: Sex Education Advisory Board for 2017/2018; 8. Business — A. Report: 2016/2017 Audit, B. Consideration: 2016/2017 Audit; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition 2.A: Troy High School Focus Hope.** Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, introduces the Mission Moment and invites Remo Roncone, Principal of Troy High School, to share about the school's Focus Hope program, recognizing the Troy High students and staff involved.

**Recognition 2.B: 2018 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists.** More than one million students nationwide from some 22,000 high schools entered the National Merit Scholarship Program; only 16,000 of these seniors are selected to be semifinalists. The Board passes a resolution commending and congratulating fifty-one Troy semifinalists.

The semifinalists are Sanjana Anil, Brinda Avutapalli, Anuja Bagri, Venkatesh Bajji, Joseph Barlow, Tejas Bolar, Michelle Cai, Tuhin Chakraborty, Annie Chen, Afriti Chinoy, Liam Clancy, Emmanuel Dannug, Manasi Desai, Allen Diao, Sahil Dogra, Raul Dutta, James Ge, Kathleen Gu, Lyndsey Gu, Claire Hao, Runxuan Jiang, Yunsoo Kim, Austin Lan, James Li, Michael Lin, Spencer Liu, Kiran Menon, Anna Mitrofan, Murali Mohan, Robert Mu, Akash Nadella, Mohnish Nadella, Andrew Nguyen, Shankar Prabhu, Ashka Pujara, Adithya Sanjay, Yusuf Uzhunnan, Muyang Wang, Angela Wang, Amanda Wewer, Jonathan Wong, Megan Worrel, Elise Xia, Ashley Xu, Zeyu Yang, Himaneesh Yerrakalva, Justin Zhang, Daniel Zheng, William Zhou, Jane Zhou and Lisa Zou.

As in the following year's packet, the roster is printed with phonetic pronunciation guides beside most names so they can be read correctly from the podium — "Sanjana Anil (Sun-juhn-ah A-nil)," "Tuhin Chakraborty (Too-hin Cha-kra-boar-tee)," "Runxuan Jiang (Run-shawn Jong)," "Himaneesh Yerrakalva (hi-MAHN YE-ruh-KAHL-vuh)," "Elise Xia (Elise Shaw)," and, for one student, a preferred English name rather than a pronunciation: "Zeyu Yang (Bill Yang)."

The resolution recites that student achievement is honored through the National Merit semifinalist and finalist recognition programs, and that National Merit students reach semifinalist status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test and earning comparable scores on the Scholastic Aptitude Test. It is signed the seventeenth day of October, 2017. The item calls fifty-one a remarkable number of semifinalists and a tribute to the staff and parents of the district, and notes copies of the resolution will be presented to the students at a reception on November 15.

A dozen of these names appear again in the October 2018 packet among that year's 54 semifinalists — James Ge, Kathleen Gu, Lyndsey Gu, Claire Hao, James Li, Spencer Liu, Shankar Prabhu, Adithya Sanjay, Muyang Wang, Angela Wang, Megan Worrel and Elise Xia — and several are also among the senior scholar athletes recognized in February 2018, indicating the same cohort of students recurring across the district's recognitions.

**Consent agenda.** Minutes of the September 5, 2017 special board meeting; minutes of the September 5, 2017 board workshop; minutes of the September 19, 2017 board meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for August 2017.

**Treasurer's Report, August 2017.** General Fund (101) check disbursements are $4,583,699.91, with Total General Fund of $4,771,055.94 and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS of $8,432,205.85. Adding ACH debits of $12,128.94, outgoing wire transfers of $1,137,361.53 and P-Card purchases of $189,355.81, and subtracting prior period void disbursements of $2,938.40, TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD is $9,768,113.73. The middle sections of the packet are the August check register run by fund.

**Curriculum 7.A: Sex Education Advisory Board membership for 2017-2018.** Districts must establish a Sex Education Advisory Board; at least one-half of the board must be parents and one of the parents must co-chair. The resolution approves the membership for the 2017/2018 school year as attached.

The board is co-chaired by Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins. School district personnel are Amy Buchanan, assistant principal at Smith Middle School; Lisa Danhoff, teacher at Troy High School; Karyn Wakely, teacher at Athens High School; Stacey Schoenherr, social worker at Smith Middle School; and Kevin Wilson, teacher at Boulan Park Middle School. Clergy is represented by Rev. Gregg Mayberry of Big Beaver United Methodist Church, 3753 John R Road; the health resource is David Roth of the Oakland Health Department, 1200 N. Telegraph Road, Pontiac.

Compared with the 2018-2019 roster adopted a year later, the composition is nearly unchanged — the same four district staff besides the co-chair, the same clergy member and the same health resource — with Kristy Pierce, by then assistant principal at Boulan Park, replacing Buchanan as the district co-chair alongside Jenkins.

**Business 8.A and 8.B: the 2016-2017 audit.** David R. Youngstrom, CPA, audit partner from Yeo & Yeo, presents the audit results for the year ended June 30, 2017; a draft copy of the district's audit report had been presented to the Board at the October workshop, and item 8.B asks the Board to accept the financial statements.

The opinion is unmodified — described as the highest level of assurance — meaning the district's financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Troy School District as of June 30, 2017 and the year then ended, in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.

The governmental funds balance sheet is presented across the General Fund, the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, nonmajor governmental funds and the total. Cash and investments are $18,111,636 in the General Fund, $37,164,463 in Capital Projects and $9,695,429 in nonmajor funds, totalling $64,971,528. Receivables net are $1,006,837, nil and $40,155, totalling $1,046,992. Due from other governmental units is $18,449,445, nil and $418,013, totalling $18,867,458. Prepaid items and inventory are $489,092, nil and $34,918, totalling $524,010. Total assets are $38,057,010, $37,164,463 and $10,188,515, totalling $85,409,988.

On liabilities, accounts payable and other liabilities are $3,096,925, $446,001 and $1,366,439, totalling $4,909,365. Accrued payroll and related liabilities are $10,243,243 in the General Fund alone. Unearned revenues are $511,451 and $453,730, totalling $965,181. Total liabilities are $13,851,619, $446,001 and $1,820,169, totalling $16,117,789.

Fund balance is broken out by constraint: non-spendable prepaid items and inventory $489,092 and $34,918, totalling $524,010; restricted for food service $1,116,618; restricted for debt service $2,643,654; restricted for capital projects $36,718,462 and $1,307,652, totalling $38,026,114; committed $1,090,947; assigned to capital projects $2,174,557; and unassigned $23,716,299 in the General Fund. Total fund balance is $24,205,391 in the General Fund, $36,718,462 in the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and $8,368,346 in nonmajor funds, for $69,292,199 in total.

The statement of revenues, expenditures and changes in fund balances for the year ended June 30, 2017 gives revenues and other sources of $146,227,426 in the General Fund, $40,136,105 in the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and $26,239,304 in nonmajor funds, totalling $212,602,835. Expenditures and other uses are $143,554,320, $3,417,643 and $36,142,175, totalling $183,114,138. The change in fund balance is accordingly $2,673,106, $36,718,462 and a decrease of $9,902,871, for a total increase of $29,488,697. Fund balance at July 1, 2016 was $21,532,285, nil and $18,271,217, totalling $39,803,502, rising to the $69,292,199 above.

The shape of that year is entirely the bond. The 2016 Capital Projects Fund did not exist at July 1, 2016; it took in $40,136,105 and spent $3,417,643, ending the year holding $36,718,462. The nonmajor funds fell $9,902,871 as the earlier capital program spent down. The General Fund's own operating result was a modest $2,673,106 surplus.

General Fund revenue including other sources: state $97,064,534, or 67%; local $38,211,378, or 26%; interdistrict sources $7,610,128, or 5%; federal $3,281,077, or 2%; and other $60,309, less than 1%. General Fund expenditures by object include employee benefits $45,172,027 and supplies and materials $17,726,062 at 12%, with capital outlay $619,824 and other $2,223,594. By function: instruction $99,214,158, or 69%; supporting services $43,617,694, or 30%; capital outlay $619,824, or 1%; and other $102,644, less than 1%.

The instructional expenditures comparison shows Troy at 69% for 2016-17, 69% for 2015-16 and 68% for 2014-15, against an average of all Oakland County schools of 63% for 2015-16 — the same six-point advantage the district would report the following year.

The per-pupil analysis of General Fund revenues, expenditures and transfers runs from 2013 to 2017: revenues $10,641, $10,812, $10,924, $11,094 and $11,353; expenses $10,585, $10,526, $10,560, $11,028 and $11,145. Revenue exceeds expense in every year of the series.

The ten-year enrollment trend runs 12,174 in 2008, 12,177, 12,076, 12,032, 12,312, 12,438, 12,591, 12,563, 12,717 and 12,881 in 2017 — the trough in 2011 and steady growth after.

The General Fund unassigned balance runs $21,433,250 in 2013, $21,000,702 in 2014, $20,231,419 in 2015, $21,038,513 in 2016 and $23,716,299 in 2017, the largest single-year increase of the series.

**Internal controls and compliance — the one qualification.** On internal controls the report finds no material weaknesses and no significant deficiencies, with management comments on federal procedures and on time and effort record keeping. (Both comments carry forward into the following year's audit, where time and effort record keeping is marked corrected and federal procedures remains in progress.)

On major federal programs the results diverge. The Special Education Cluster receives an unmodified opinion. The Nutrition Cluster receives a **qualified opinion**, with a **material weakness for excess fund balance** and a **significant deficiency for student eligibility**.

This is the only qualification in the report and the only one in either the 2017 or 2018 audit as carried in these packets — by the following year both federal clusters would receive unmodified opinions with no material weaknesses, no significant deficiencies and no material noncompliance. The excess fund balance finding is a specific federal constraint: school food service programs may not accumulate a surplus beyond a set limit, and the balance sheet in this same presentation shows $1,116,618 restricted for food service. The student eligibility deficiency concerns the determination of which students qualify for free and reduced-price meals. Read together with the March 2018 budget amendment, which added a $100,000 repairs and rentals line to the Food Service Fund where the original budget had none, the district's response to carrying too much food service money appears to have been to start spending it.

**Future challenges.** The auditor lists the state economic and political condition, rising fringe benefit costs, the retirement rate increase, and eroding state revenue sources. The following year's list would replace "eroding state revenue sources" with two hard numbers — a post-employment benefit obligation of nearly $77M and a net pension liability of over $225.2M.

Read as a whole, the October 2017 packet is the district's annual reckoning, and it reads well: an unmodified opinion, a clean internal control report, 69% of spending on instruction against a county average of 63%, per-pupil revenue exceeding per-pupil expense in every year of a five-year series, an unassigned balance up nearly $2.7 million, enrollment at a ten-year high, and fifty-one National Merit semifinalists. The single blemish is a federal food service program holding more money than the rules allow.

## Meeting

Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 p.m., April 9, 2013, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public comment is limited to one-half hour each for agenda and non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

## Recognition

Spirit of Diversity Awards, in their first year and designed by the Troy Diversity Council, honor sixteen groups and individuals including Padma Kuppa, Rouba Samman, Jen Hilzinger, Nadeen Brown, Tonia Romancheck, the Troy African American Parent Network, Bemis Cultural Coffee, Jesse Allgeier, and the Troy High head peer mediators led by teacher Gail Yax. Ten teachers were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher program; Laurie Pickell (Martell) was named district Teacher of the Year and receives a free one-year car lease donated by the Suburban Collection, with Patrick Koneval (Smith) and Omar Hakim (International Academy East) also sent to Oakland Schools. The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, led by president Al Robinson, funded 114 mini-grants, a record for a single year. Jason Brolus presents Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union cash grants.

## Minutes on the consent agenda

The February 5, 2013 meeting adopted Resolutions 13-018 through 13-025, each 7-0: new hires; a two-year probationary administrative contract for Mark Washington as Director of Technology effective February 11, 2013; closing Athens and Troy High to open enrollment for 2013/2014 except not more than 25 ninth graders; authorization to prepare an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds; a 2012/2013 budget amendment; a $44,768.00 web filter award to Phantom Technologies; and second reading of policy K-1303. The March 19 special meeting adopted Resolution 13-026 for closed session on negotiations, 7-0.

## Reports and action items

- Elementary and middle school mathematics materials adoption, reported by math coordinator Kris Karbon; middle school teachers trialed Big Ideas Math, while the Algebra 1 - Geometry - Algebra 2 sequence will make a materials recommendation next spring.
- Fall 2012 MEAP results, reported by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment: Troy's combined-grade proficiency was 87% reading, 77% math, 57% social studies and 27% science.

Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 p.m. on April 9, 2013 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, telephone 248.823.4000, with meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda runs from the Pledge of Allegiance through recognitions, additions and deletions, public communication, the general consent agenda, personnel, curriculum, business, other, closed session and adjournment.

RECOGNITION. The Spirit of Diversity Awards, in their first year and designed by the Troy Diversity Council, honor sixteen groups and individuals: Padma Kuppa; Rouba Samman and Jen Hilzinger for the Schroeder World Tour; Nadeen Brown, president of the Troy African American Parent Network; Tonia Romancheck; TAAPN, whose leaders include Aretha Bradley, Constance Dansby, Tesha Long and Cathy Hodges and whose Saturday Excel math series and tutoring carry the motto "Look for greatness in each child and you will find it"; Jen Hilzinger for Cultural Coffee hours at Boulan Park Middle School; the Troy High head peer mediators - Nico Adamski, Nicholas Arsanos, Connor Hayden, Hope Keating, Justin Losey, Miranda Mio, Thomas O'Donovan, Alexsys Pullen, Rebecca Ress, Rachel Sacco and Eve Theoharis - led by teacher Gail Yax, a group that trains more than 300 students annually; Bemis Cultural Coffee PTO members Jeanette Tanafranca, Vicki Wind, Janice Girling, Mehrun-nisa Ahmad and Kendra Cooper; and Jesse Allgeier for more than three years on the Troy Diversity Project. Honorable mentions go to the Athens Theatre Company, Sandra LewAllen, Tom Wylie, Brian Nutting, Marlene Seltzer, M.D., and Joe Thilman of PFLAG. Ten teachers were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award Program; seven were honored - Nancy Haboush (Leonard), Elizabeth Mayne (Hamilton), Lynn Mui (Wattles), Jessica Thudium (Hamilton), Karen Muzljakovich (Morse), Faith Clay (Bemis) and Alan Gieleghem (Wattles) - and three were forwarded to Oakland Schools by a TEA selection committee: Laurie Pickell (Martell), Patrick Koneval (Smith Middle School) and Omar Hakim (International Academy East). Pickell was also named the district's Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year lease of a car donated by the Suburban Collection. The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, whose president Al Robinson speaks while Karen Rockwell rolls recipients on screen, funded 114 grants this year, a record number in a single year. Jason Brolus of Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union, which sponsored a pre-meeting reception, presents cash grant awards.

MINUTES. The February 5, 2013 regular meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, Superintendent Fowler and administrators Keeling, Lesser, Machesky, Rajter and Witt attending, and roughly 22 audience members. Resolution 13-018 approved the consent agenda; 13-019 hired Zachary MacIntosh, Letitia Mason, Megan Sulewski and Leah Vohs; 13-020 gave Mark Washington a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Technology effective February 11, 2013; 13-021 closed Athens High and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2013/2014 except for not more than 25 ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area, with Dr. Machesky noting the option's fourth year and consistent uptake of 22 to 23 students; 13-022 authorized preparation of an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds under the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, certified by Secretary Paula Fleming under Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976; 13-023 amended the 2012/2013 appropriations to $131,488,075 General Fund, $8,805,399 Special Revenue, $18,113,148 Debt Service, $290,713 Capital Projects and $25,000 Internal Service; 13-024 awarded the web filter bid to Phantom Technologies for $44,768.00; and 13-025 approved changes to policy K-1303, Commercial Advertising. All votes were 7-0. Enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants were presented at three levels. Elliot Gould announced Troy Youth Assistance's "Dollars for Education" 50/50 raffle, $25 per ticket with only 2,000 sold and a drawing April 25. Student representatives Patty Durell (Troy High), Aishawarya Singh (Athens, Charity Week goal $28,000 for Angels of Hope) and Miranda Wilson (Niles) reported; the meeting adjourned at 7:53 p.m. The February 12 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 10:40 p.m.; the March 19 workshop ran 6:10 p.m. to 7:43 p.m. with Mr. Schmidt participating by remote communications; the March 19 special meeting adopted Resolution 13-026 to enter closed session on negotiations by roll call, 7-0, at 7:54 p.m., adjourning at 9:20 p.m.

The February summary, dated April 2, 2013, shows General Fund $2,499,544.27, Special Revenue $72,150.43 and Other Funds $80,541.91 for total checks of $2,652,236.61, ACH debits $48,498.27, wire transfers $2,109,992.75, P-Card purchases $154,890.98 and voids of $(1,753.28), totaling $4,963,865.33.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of October 20, 2020, held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, and livestreamed via Zoom Webinar, presented for approval as item 5.B on the November 17, 2020 agenda. The Board honored fifty-two 2021 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, accepted the district's audited 2020 financial statements from Plante Moran, and approved purchases from Presidio Networked Solutions Group and IMBranded. The most contentious action was a disclaiming motion stating that the actions of Trustee Hammond are not the actions of the Troy Board of Education, adopted on a 4-3 roll call.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
Meeting and attendance
- Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, October 20, 2020, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, livestreamed via Zoom Webinar with public notice posted so community members could participate remotely.
- President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:10 p.m.; the start was delayed by technical/audio difficulties. The meeting adjourned at 11:38 p.m.
- Board members physically present with Mr. Schmidt: Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Pagel, and West.
- Approximately 75 additional members of the audience attended via Zoom Webinar, along with four student representatives to the Board and Donna Hanson and Michael Walsh of Plante Moran.
- Minutes respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (GH/jh).

Recognition
- TSD Mission Moment: Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, introduced the TSD CARE Company, recognizing Tim Fulcher, Dawn Wyatt, and CARE Co. staff for providing childcare to TSD staff while many centers were closed during the pandemic. Dawn Wyatt recognized Sui Chu, Gina Kitchen, Ally Larkins, and Linda Smith, and thanked Dr. Erin Detmer for providing space at Leonard Elementary School.
- 2021 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists: Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, reported that more than one million students nationwide from some 21,000 high schools entered the program and only 16,000 seniors are selected as semifinalists. A resolution honored fifty-two Troy semifinalists, who reached that status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT. Copies were to be presented at a virtual reception on November 4th; the resolution was signed the twentieth day of October 2020 and adopted 7-0.
- Michigan Association of School Boards awards: Board Secretary Gary Hauff received the President's Award, the highest level of achievement, requiring 29 advanced classes and a minimum of 1,383 education credits; Don Wotruba, Executive Director of MASB in Lansing, presented it in Troy. Trustee Dr. Nancy Philippart was recognized for 12 years of service.

Numbered actions
| Res. | Item | Vote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20-076 | Consent agenda items A through I | 7-0 |
| 20-077 | Personnel recommendations (new hires) | 7-0 |
| 20-078 | TESA/MEA/NEA tentative agreement ratification | 7-0 |
| 20-079 | Audited 2020 financial statements accepted | 7-0 |
| 20-080 | Adult Education technology purchase, $54,456.00 | 7-0 |
| 20-081 | PPE purchase, $44,851.80 | 7-0 |
| 20-082 | Reconfirmation of COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan | 6-1 |
| 20-083 | Disclaiming motion regarding Trustee Hammond | 4-3 |

Other business
- Mrs. Hammond asked that the Reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan be removed from the consent agenda; Mr. Schmidt moved it to Other.
- Public communication: Katie Gorman, Joe Pettinato, Amber Barbieri, and Alec Peeples, all residents of Troy, addressed the Board on the Hamilton principal and staff, Board ethics, transparency, and support for teachers.
- Plante Moran presented the 2019-2020 fiscal year audit, first shown in draft at the October 16th Board Workshop, reporting no findings or questioned costs.
- Superintendent's update featured elementary and secondary principals describing in-seat and remote learning.
- Student representatives Nathania Nartey (Athens High), Pranay Gupta (International Academy-East), and Sejal Patil (Troy High) reported; Carlton Thomas (Troy College & Career High School) was not present.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
Minutes of the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education held October 20, 2020 in the Services Building at 4420 Livernois and livestreamed via Zoom Webinar, with a public notice posted to allow community members to participate remotely. The minutes were placed on the November 17, 2020 Board agenda as item 5.B for approval.

Call to order and attendance. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:10 p.m.; the start was delayed due to technical/audio difficulties. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members physically present were Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Pagel, and West. Approximately 75 additional members of the audience were present via Zoom Webinar, as well as four student representatives to the Board and Donna Hanson and Michael Walsh from Plante Moran.

Recognition - TSD Mission Moment: CARE Company Staff. Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, introduced the TSD CARE Company as the month's Mission Moment. She recognized Tim Fulcher, Dawn Wyatt, and the CARE Co. staff and thanked them for providing quality childcare service to TSD staff members, noting that many childcare centers were closed due to the pandemic. Dawn Wyatt introduced her team and recognized Sui Chu, Gina Kitchen, Ally Larkins, and Linda Smith, and thanked Dr. Erin Detmer for providing the space in Leonard Elementary School to hold the program.

Recognition - 2021 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists. Mrs. Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, announced that more than one million students nationwide from some 21,000 high schools entered the National Merit Scholarship Program, and that only 16,000 of these seniors are selected as semifinalists. The resolution recited that National Merit students reach semifinalist status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test (PSAT) and earning comparable scores on the Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT). Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart, the Board adopted a resolution commending fifty-two Troy School District semifinalists: Nina Aitas, Harika Billa, Marcus Chung, Poulomi Dey, Sneha Dinda, Prashanti Donthireddy, Alaina Favret, Archita Girmannagari, Annie He, Madhavan Iyengar, Diksha Iyer, Shruti Jain, Mahith Kanuri, Achyuth Kashyap, Arjun Kashyap, Raj Khuperkar, Heeweon Kim, Minseong Kim, Armol Kirtane, Krishna Kottai, Nathan Kovacs, Sophia Liang, Elliot Liu, Shifa Malik, Sandhya Manivasagam, Esha Munagala, Parvathi Nagappala, Kishan Patel, Aarti Phatke, Prajna Polamarasetti, Lauryn Prokup, Sohil Ramachandra, Navneet Ramadurai, Swarith Reddy, Surya Sanjay, Nicholas Simon, Sabrina Song, Matthew Villavicencio, Sohan Vittalam, Allison Wei, Josiah Wong, Jasmine Wu, Alexander Xu, Sarah Xu, Lily Yang, Ruicheng Yang, Dorothy Yin, Michael Young, Darren Zeng, Anna Zhao, Katherine Zhao, and Erik Zhou. Copies of the resolution were to be presented to the students at a virtual reception on November 4th. The resolution was signed this twentieth day of October 2020 and carried on a roll call with Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, and Hauff all voting Yes.

Recognition - Michigan Association of School Boards awards. The Board honored Secretary Gary Hauff for receiving the President's Award, described as the highest level of achievement, which requires a Board member to complete 29 advanced classes and a minimum of 1,383 education credits. Don Wotruba, Executive Director of the Michigan Association of School Boards in Lansing, came to Troy to honor Mr. Hauff with the award Friday morning. Trustee Dr. Nancy Philippart was recognized for 12 years of dedicated service on the Board.

Additions and deletions. Mrs. Hammond requested that the Reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan be removed from the consent agenda and placed as a regular agenda item for discussion; Mr. Schmidt agreed to move that item to Other.

Public communication. Katie Gorman, resident of Troy, spoke about the Hamilton principal and the job the staff is doing keeping students safe, and said discussion at the last Board meeting should have been conducted in closed session rather than a public meeting. Joe Pettinato, resident of Troy, expressed appreciation for the Board's response during the past few months and mentioned Elizabeth Hammond's leadership and engagement. Amber Barbieri, resident of Troy, addressed Board ethics and thanked Mrs. Hammond for advocating on residents' behalf. Alec Peeples, resident of Troy, addressed transparency and ethics and asked for support of open public discourse.

General - consent agenda, resolution 20-076. Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Gottlieb, the Board approved items A through I: A. Minutes of the September 1, 2020 Board of Education Workshop; B. Minutes of the September 1, 2020 Special Board of Education Meeting; C. Minutes of the September 15, 2020 Board of Education Meeting; D. Minutes of the September 15, 2020 Closed Session Meeting; E. Minutes of the September 29, 2020 Special Board of Education Meeting; F. Treasurer's Report - August 2020; G. Oakland County CARES Act Distribution Interlocal Agreement; H. Safe-Ed Contract Extension; and I. Clean-Ed Contract Extension. Roll call: Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, and Philippart Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

Personnel, resolution 20-077. The Board approved the personnel recommendations as stated, with new hires Breanna Thacker, Nicole Wilson, Hannah Tout, Jodie Seilheimer, and Emily Surzyn. Roll call: Wilson, Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Schmidt Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

TESA contract extension, resolution 20-078. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Hammond, the Board ratified and adopted the tentative agreement reached on September 30, 2020 between representatives of the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA for the period of July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2024. Roll call: Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, and Wilson Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

Business - 2019/2020 Audit Report, resolution 20-079. Ms. Donna Hanson and Mr. Michael Walsh from Plante Moran presented on the audit of the 2019-2020 fiscal year; a draft copy of the District's Audit Report had been presented in detail to the Board at the October 16th Board Workshop. They reported there were no findings or questioned costs. Governmental funds revenue and expenditures were reviewed, as well as student population and foundation allowance. The economic impact of the pandemic and MPSERS challenges, and changes in federal funding such as the Coronavirus Relief Funds, Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Relief Funds, and Child Care Relief Funds, were discussed at length. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Gottlieb, the Board accepted and approved the Troy School District's audited 2020 financial statements as presented by Plante Moran. Roll call: Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, and Wilson Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

Adult Education Technology Purchase, resolution 20-080. The Board approved the purchase of laptops and carts from Presidio Networked Solutions Group in the amount of $54,456.00, approved as an expenditure of the General Fund. Roll call: Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, and Anne Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PPE Purchase, resolution 20-081. The Board approved the purchase of acrylic shields and graphics from IMBranded in the amount of $44,851.80, approved as an expenditure of the General Fund. Roll call: Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, and Gottlieb Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

Superintendent's update. Dr. Machesky asked Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, and Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction, to share an update on learning at both the elementary and secondary level. Ms. Griffor introduced Bemis Principal Jeremey Whan, Hill Principal Shari Pawlus, Leonard Principal Dr. Erin Detmer, and Morse Principal Stephanie Zendler, who gave examples of learning happening in their buildings. Ms. DiPilato introduced Smith Principal Chris Mueller and Boulan Park Principal Tony Morse to describe how middle school students had transitioned back to in-seat learning. Further discussion followed among Board and administration about students returning to in-seat and remote learning.

Reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness & Response Plan, resolution 20-082. Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 provides a structure to support Michigan schools planning for the return of Pre-K through Post High School education in the fall; under the order districts must adopt a COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan addressing the phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan, submit a reconfirmation plan to the Board monthly, and post the Preparedness Plan on the district website home page for public access. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Dr. Wilson, the Board approved the District's Reconfirmation. Roll call: Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Anne, and Gottlieb Yes; Hammond No. Yes: 6, No: 1.

Reports from student representatives. Nathania Nartey, Student Representative for Athens High School; Pranay Gupta, Student Representative for the International Academy-East; and Sejal Patil, Student Representative for Troy High School, each shared updates. Carlton Thomas, Student Representative for Troy College & Career High School, was not present.

Board member ethics violation, resolution 20-083. Dr. Wilson and Dr. Philippart shared a PowerPoint presentation explaining the role of a Board member, covering Board governance, the National School Boards Association Code of Ethics, the Code of Ethics outlined in the TSD Policy Manual, censure, and disclaiming acts of individual Board members. They presented examples of an ethics violation and provided excerpts of social media posts and a letter from the Troy Education Association, stating that given social media posts made by Trustee Hammond, who is seen as a representative of the Board, the community's interpretation of recent actions may be misconstrued as representing the Board and District. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Dr. Wilson, the motion declared that the actions of Trustee Hammond are not the actions of the Troy Board of Education and that the community be alerted that unless specifically authorized by motion of the Board, Trustee Hammond's opinions and actions are as an individual community member and should not be construed as representing the Troy Board of Education. Mr. Schmidt gave each Board member the opportunity to speak before voting. Roll call: Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, and Hauff Yes; Anne, Gottlieb, and Hammond No. Yes: 4, No: 3.

Adjournment. The meeting adjourned at 11:38 p.m. Respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (GH/jh).

Solicitation
- Bid No. 9909, Exterior Signage at Athens High School, Learning Center and Early Childcare Center, Troy School District. Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083.
- Specifications available through the district website under Business Services / Purchasing and posted on BuildingConnected at https://app.buildingconnected.com/public/5f0dc09564fd95003450f194 by November 4, 2020 at 5:00 PM local time.
- Sealed bids submitted only through BuildingConnected; no physical, oral, email, telephonic, or telegraphic proposals. Due no later than 11:00 AM Wednesday, November 4, 2020; public opening immediately after via meet.google.com/dns-ibvf-oif.

The invitation sets a question deadline of noon, Wednesday, October 28, 2020 (fax 248.823.4077, email PurchasingOffice@troy.k12.mi.us), while Instruction 4 states questions must be received no later than noon, Wednesday, November 28, 2020. Instruction 1 also carries over language referring to Bid No. 9906 Niles Center Demolition.

Work scope
| Site | Address | Work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Troy Learning Center | 1522 Big Beaver Road, Troy, MI 48083 | New exterior signage |
| Troy Early Childhood Care | 201 West Square Lake Road, Troy, MI 48098 | New exterior signage |
| Athens High School | 4333 John R Road, Troy, MI 48085 | Remove and replace exterior signage; masonry structure maintained and modified as required |

The contractor is responsible for excavation and concrete, City and State permits, final electrical connection, COVID-19 procedures per the Troy School District website and Oakland County, removal of soil spoils, site restoration, and waste removal. The base bid must include a $5,000 allowance at the Owner's discretion. Electrical is excluded. The proposal form breaks out Athens High School, Learning Center, Early Childcare Center, Base Bid, and Bond amounts and requires five recent references.

Bidding requirements
- Bid bond or certified check for not less than five percent of the bid; unsuccessful bidders' security returned within ten days.
- Performance and payment bonds of 100% of the bid for proposals of $50,000 or more per MCL 129.201; bond company must be a Michigan licensed carrier with an excellent or superior AM Best rating.
- Notarized familial disclosure per MCL 380.1267 and Iran Economic Sanctions Act certification under Public Act 517 of 2012; false certification carries a civil penalty of not more than $250,000.00 or two times the contract amount, whichever is greater, plus three years of bid ineligibility.

- Insurance: Employer's Liability, Comprehensive General Liability, Owner's Contractor's Protective, and Automobile Liability each at $1,000,000, with 60 days written notice of change or cancellation.
- Criminal history and background checks required under MCL 380.1230 et seq. for personnel on district premises more than one continuous week.

Technical specification

- LED message centers, basis of design Thinksign Model Xtreme V-2 16 mm display, or Daktronics, Spectrum, or approved equal; full color, 4.4" character height, minimum 60 pixel rows by 150 pixel columns, IP-67 sealed modules, 4G or 5G lifetime cellular communications.

Complete bid package issued by the Troy School District Purchasing Department for Bid No. 9909, Exterior Signage at Athens High School, Learning Center and Early Childcare Center. The package contains the Invitation to Bid, Instructions to Bidders, scope of work, proposal form, familial disclosure and Iran Economic Sanctions certifications, acceptance of proposal form, and the Division-level Exterior Signage technical specification, followed by aerial location imagery.

Invitation to Bid. The Troy School District will receive firm, sealed bids for all labor, material, equipment and all other services to complete Bid No. 9909. Specifications and proposal forms are obtainable online at http://www.troy.k12.mi.us under the Business Services tab, then Purchasing. Bid documents were to be placed on BuildingConnected at https://app.buildingconnected.com/public/5f0dc09564fd95003450f194 by November 4, 2020 at 5:00 PM local time. Sealed bids must be submitted through that BuildingConnected link; no physical bids are accepted, and no oral, email, telephonic or telegraphic proposals are considered. Bids were due no later than 11:00 AM Wednesday, November 4, 2020, and publicly opened immediately following the close of receiving bids at the virtual meeting link meet.google.com/dns-ibvf-oif. No pre-bid walk through was scheduled. Questions were to be submitted in writing only and answered by addendum to all interested parties, with the invitation setting a deadline of noon, Wednesday October 28, 2020, questions faxed to 248.823.4077 or emailed as a Word document to PurchasingOffice@troy.k12.mi.us. The Instructions to Bidders section carries a conflicting statement that questions must be received no later than noon, Wednesday, November 28, 2020, and its opening paragraph retains boilerplate referring to Bid No. 9906 Niles Center Demolition. The issuing office is the Purchasing Department, Troy School District, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083. The recommendation for award was to be submitted to the Board of Education at the regular Board of Education meeting to be held on Tuesday, November 17, 2020.

Statutory and bonding requirements. All bidders must provide familial disclosure in compliance with MCL 380.1267, attached to the bid proposal as a sworn and notarized statement disclosing any familial relationship between the owner or any employee of the bidder and any member of the Troy School Board or the Troy School District's Superintendent. A sworn and notarized affidavit of compliance for the Iran Economic Sanctions Act, certifying compliance with Public Act 517 of 2012, must accompany all proposals; a false certification carries a civil penalty of not more than $250,000.00 or two times the amount of the contract or proposed contract, whichever is greater, plus the cost of the District's investigation and reasonable attorney fees, and renders the person ineligible to bid for three years. In accordance with Michigan Compiled Laws Section 129.201, successful bidders whose proposals are $50,000 or more for any bid category must furnish a U.S. Treasury Listed Company Performance and Payment Bond in the amount of 100% of their bid, with the cost of the bond identified within each proposal. A bid bond or certified check for not less than five percent of the bid amount must accompany each bid; the security of each unsuccessful bidder is returned within ten days after award. A performance bond is required if the project cost exceeds $50,000 and must be listed separately on the proposal form as an individual line item. Within fourteen days after written notice of selection, treated as notice to proceed, the successful bidder must enter into a contract and file bonds equal to 100% of the full contract sum, from a bond company listed by the State of Michigan as a licensed carrier with an excellent or superior rating from AM Best Company. The Troy Board of Education reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids in whole or in part, to award to other than the low bidder, and to waive irregularities.

Bidder qualifications and commercial terms. Bidders must be reputable, recognized organizations with at least five years of successful experience on work of this type and scope. Material and equipment are guaranteed free from defects in workmanship and materials for no less than two years from date of receipt or installation, with manufacturer warranty prevailing where longer, and defective items replaced or repaired within seven working days at vendor expense. No proposal may be withdrawn until after 45 days after bid opening; the acceptance of proposal form states the undersigned will execute a contract if notified of acceptance within thirty days after opening. The successful bidder holds bid prices firm for all purchase orders for approximately one full year. The contractor obtains and pays for all permits, assessments, fees and other charges, and provides the District all permit paperwork at completion. Troy School District is not automatically exempt from State of Michigan Sales and Use Taxes; taxes on materials permanently attached or incorporated into realty are paid by the vendor.

Insurance and safety. The contractor must maintain Worker's Compensation Insurance with statutory limits and Employer's Liability Insurance with a minimum limit of $1,000,000 each occurrence; Comprehensive General Liability with a minimum combined single limit of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate, endorsed for sixty days written notice of material change, cancellation or non-renewal; an Owner's Contractor's Protective Policy in the name of the Owner at a minimum combined single limit of $1,000,000 per occurrence; and Automobile Liability covering owned, hired and non-owned vehicles at a minimum combined single limit of $1,000,000 each occurrence under the Michigan no-fault Insurance Law. Policies must be issued by domestic on-shore companies licensed in Michigan with an A rating by AM Best. Compliance is required with the School Safety Initiative Legislation, MCL 380.1230, 80.1230a, 380.1230c, 380.1230d and 380.1230g; all installation personnel including subcontractors working on District premises more than one continuous week must undergo criminal history and background checks within a year of the beginning of the project, at the bidder's expense, with written documentation verifying that no personnel have a listed offense. The listed offenses enumerated include MCL 750.145a, 750.145b, 750.145c, 750.158, 750.167(1)(f), 750.335a, 750.338, 750.338a, 750.338b, 750.349, 750.350, 750.448, 750.455, 750.520b, 750.520c, 750.520d, 750.520e, 750.520g, and 750.10a. Additional provisions cover termination by the District for convenience, Equal Opportunity Employer status under Executive Order 11246, the Michigan Right to Know Law, the EPA Asbestos Hazard Emergency Response Act contractor notification forms, and presumed lead-containing materials requiring compliance with 29 CFR Part 1926.62 of the OSHA Lead Construction Standard, Part 603 of the Michigan State Standards, at contractor expense.

Work scope. The bid covers exterior signage at Athens High School, Learning Center and Early Childcare Center, on a line item lump sum basis: new exterior signage at Troy Learning Center, 1522 Big Beaver Road, Troy, MI 48083; new exterior signage at Troy Early Childhood Care, 201 West Square Lake Road, Troy, MI 48098; and removal and replacement of exterior signage at Athens High School, 4333 John R Road, Troy, MI 48085, where the masonry structure will be maintained and modified as required for proper installation. The contractor is responsible for all necessary excavation and concrete, all permits from City and State, final electrical connection to the sign, coordination with the Owner so as not to affect the buildings or operations, compliance with COVID-19 procedures noted on the Troy School District website and Oakland County, removal of soil spoils, concrete clean up and site restoration, and removal of all waste from the site. The base bid must include an allowance of $5,000 to be used at the Owner's discretion. Electrical is an excluded item. The proposal form requires separate amounts for Athens High School, Learning Center, Early Childcare Center, Base Bid and Bond, plus five recent references, preferably school districts.

Exterior signage specification. The section covers internally illuminated pylon signs and LED message centers, with delegated design by a qualified professional engineer for sign structure and anchorage. Structural performance requires a wind load of 120 MPH (3 sec gust) and thermal movement allowance for a temperature change of 120 deg F ambient and 180 deg F material surfaces; accessibility complies with ICC A117.1 and electrical components are listed and labeled as defined in NFPA 70. Verification samples include pylon sign samples not less than 12 inches square and 8-inch variable component material samples. The special warranty period is five years from date of Substantial Completion, covering deterioration of finishes beyond normal weathering, deterioration of embedded graphic image, delamination of sheet materials, and failure of the LED message center display.

Pylon signs use a basis of design of ASI Sign Systems, Inc., ASI Signage Innovations, 8181 Jetstar Drive, Suite 100, Irving, Texas 75063, as two-sided custom fabricated, internally illuminated aluminum pylon signs with backlighted LED construction, power at 120 V, 60 Hz, 1 phase, 15 A, weep holes, computer cut panels with push through white acrylic lettering, and a box depth of 1'-6". Aluminum panels meet ASTM B209, alloy EN 5052 H12, minimum 0.05 inch (1.25mm) thick; extrusions meet ASTM B221, alloy 6063-T5. Finishes are a two-phase high temperature cured polyester color coating with a 2 mil thick chromium primer layer and a two-component, water-based, non-toxic, lead-free, zero emissions top coat, with LTV series die cut vinyl or surface screen process graphics.

LED message centers use a basis of design of Thinksign Model Xtreme V-2 16 mm display, or Daktronics, Spectrum, or approved equal. New display housing dimensions are approximately 3'-8" tall by 7'-4" wide and retrofit housings approximately 4'-2" tall by 7'-4" wide, with front-to-back depth not exceeding 7 inches. Maximum display power shall not exceed 1000 watts at full drive current; displays operate from 120/240 VAC, 60 Hz single-phase, in ambient temperatures of -40 to +120 degrees F and 95% humidity. The full LED matrix measures a minimum of 60 pixel rows high by 150 pixel columns wide, full color, 16mm pitch, 4.4 inch character height, pixel configuration of 1 red, 1 green and 1 blue, with modules and power supplies fully encapsulated and sealed to IP-67 standards, no less than a 140 degree horizontal half-intensity viewing angle and 160 degree horizontal readability angle. Controllers run independently of a controlling computer, connect to light and temperature sensors, store presentations and schedules in non-volatile memory, and include a 4G or 5G lifetime cellular communications package with the manufacturer's latest LED message center software.

Materials and installation. Steel materials include ASTM A653/A653M sheet, ASTM A36/A36M or A529/A529M shapes, ASTM A529/A529M or A572/A572M plate or bar stock at 42,000-psi minimum yield strength, ASTM A500/A500M Grade B tubing, and ASTM A307 or A325 bolts; acrylic sheet meets ASTM D4802 Type UVF, polycarbonate ASTM C1349 Appendix X1 Type II, bituminous paint ASTM D1187/D1187M, and nonshrink nonmetallic grout ASTM C1107/C1107M. Aluminum posts are 0.125-inch thick extruded tubing and steel posts minimum 0.120-inch thick tubing, hot-dip galvanized per ASTM A123/A123M; direct burial posts are fabricated 42 inches longer than the height of the sign. Posts and pylons are set plumb within a tolerance of 1/16 inch in 3 feet; unsuitable subgrade is excavated an additional 12 inches and backfilled in 6-inch compacted lifts; preformed holes in concrete foundations are not less than 3/4 inch larger than the outside dimension of the post. LED displays must be grounded per Article 250 of the National Electrical Code. The package closes with aerial location imagery credited to Maxar Technologies, U.S. Geological Survey and Google, dated 2020 with image capture September 2018, labeled 201 W Square Lake Rd and 4200 John R Rd.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of February 27, 2018 at the Services Building. It sets the district's enrollment posture for 2018-2019 against Fred Ignatovich's projection of 13,207 students — closing Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder, Boulan Park and both high schools to open enrollment except for up to 25 incoming ninth graders transferring to Athens, while opening a limited Schools of Choice program for 40 kindergarten, 3 first grade and 14 middle school seats. Business awards $55,865.00 of fiber maintenance to Fiber Link, Inc. and $188,971.00 of general trades work to R&E Development, and the December 2017 Treasurer's Report carries total disbursements in period of $13,132,669.57.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting, February 27, 2018, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
Four items: the 2017-2018 Senior Scholar Athletes, who must maintain a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program; the Fall 2017 All-State Athletes; a Mission Moment on the Troy High Auto Lab with David Easterbrook; and Principal Appreciation Month, marked by a resolution recognizing February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy.

**Consent agenda**
Six items: minutes of the December 5, 2017 closed session, the January 9, 2018 special meeting, the January 9 closed session and the January 9 workshop, minutes of the January 16, 2018 organizational and regular meeting, and the December 2017 Treasurer's Report.

**Treasurer's Report — December 2017**
Total check disbursements are $10,949,972.44 — General Fund $9,978,994.82, Special Revenue Funds $248,358.87 and Other Funds $722,618.75 — and total disbursements in period are $13,132,669.57, including $1,972,883.34 of outgoing wire transfers, $179,070.01 of P-Card purchases and $33,022.78 of ACH debits. Within the fund breakdown, the General Fund (101) alone accounts for $9,468,981.45. (The transmittal's period line reads "December, 2018" as printed, though the registers themselves are December 2017.)

**The January 16 minutes, in brief**
The organizational meeting elected Mr. Schmidt president, Mr. Gottlieb vice president and Mr. Hauff secretary, each 6-0 with Mrs. Hammond absent, ending Dr. Philippart's seven years as president. Rick L. West was appointed treasurer for January through December 2018, twelve depository institutions named, six law firms continued as counsel, and Judy Holmes designated to post meeting notices. The Board also ratified the TESPA contract extension through June 30, 2022 and approved the $853,231.22 furniture purchase for 4th and 5th grade classrooms. Mr. Schmidt explained on the record that the corrected asbestos resolution "was just an error naming the company that was awarded the bid" — the consulting firm's name had been inadvertently used in the original.

**Curriculum — who may enroll in 2018-2019**
Dr. Machesky presents enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants. District headcount has climbed from 11,965 in 2005/06 to **13,084 in 2017/18**, and the projection for 2018/19 is **13,207**, rising to 13,274, 13,320, 13,325 and 13,396 through 2022/23. Actual enrollment has run ahead of both the projected and budgeted figures in each of the last three years — 13,084 actual against 12,992 projected and 12,900 budgeted in 2017/18.

On that basis administration recommends closing Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder and Boulan Park on total enrollment and space constraints, and closing Athens and Troy High again — with the exception of **not more than 25 incoming ninth grade students** who live in the Troy High attendance area but wish to attend Athens, applications accepted during a two-week window at the beginning of March. Students with siblings at Athens or Troy High in grades 9 through 11 may open enroll to remain.

Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent of Teaching and Learning, presents the Schools of Choice report first given at the February 6 workshop. Of the district's elementary students, **500 are Schools of Choice against 5,096 non-SOC — 8.93%**, ranging from 19.05% at Hill and 15.70% at Costello down to 0.95% at Schroeder. A survey of current SOC families found 40 kindergarten, 3 first grade and 14 middle school siblings planning to attend. Kris Griffor and Mark Dziatczak's February 6 memo recommends exactly those numbers, noting that on the prior year's application volume the district anticipates far more than 50 kindergarten applicants and could admit more in the third week of August if space allows.

Four separate resolutions follow, splitting each grade band between Section 105 (districts within Oakland County) and Section 105c (districts outside Oakland County whose ISD is contiguous with Oakland ISD): 40 kindergarten and 3 first grade under each of 105 and 105c, and 14 total 6th-8th grade students at Baker, Larson and Smith under each — the counts being the same students viewed from either statute, not additive.

**Business**

| Item | Award | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fiber maintenance (Bid #9851) | Fiber Link, Inc. — $55,865.00 | General Fund |
| General trades, BP 21A | R&E Development — $188,971.00 | 2016 Capital Projects Fund |

Three fiber proposals came in — Amcomm at $75,791.00, Fiber Link at $45,865.00 and Turnkey Network Solutions at $29,651.62. John Foster of Convergent Technology Partners recommends Fiber Link despite Turnkey's lower base bid, because Turnkey underestimated the work and its higher hourly rates would exhaust a time-and-materials contract faster. The award adds Voluntary Alternates for CAD prints of the outside and building fiber routes ($7,500.00 and $2,500.00) to reach $55,865.00. The service is newly eligible for E-rate Category 1 reimbursement of roughly 40%.

The general trades package covers roller shades, window sills, platform and ceiling work at Costello, Leonard, Martell and Morse, plus remodel work at Troy Union and hollow metal doors at Troy High, Athens and IA East. Barton Malow disqualified low bidder Titan Retail Industries for omitting a required allowance and, after a post-bid interview, recommended R&E Development at $188,971.00.

**Other**
The Board adopts its 2018 committee assignments, approves Vice President Steve Gottlieb's attendance at the NSBA Annual Conference in San Antonio, April 7-9, 2018, and casts its ballot in the MASB Region 8 election among Donald Hubler (incumbent, Macomb ISD), Robert McLachlan, Birgit McQuiston and Darlene Pomponio, Ph.D.

**Recognition 2.A: Senior Scholar Athletes 2017-2018.** The Board welcomes and acknowledges senior scholar athletes from winter and spring sports; to achieve the distinction a student must maintain a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program. The packet prints the full roster of roughly 115 seniors by name, sport and school across Athens and Troy High — cross country, football, boys and girls soccer, boys tennis, girls golf, girls swim and dive, volleyball and fall cheerleading.

**Recognition 2.B: All-State Athletes, Fall 2017.** Ten students are named all-state in their sports, read out by Mr. Jolly: Gabriel Brown (freshman, Athens, tennis), Brennan Cimpeanu (sophomore, Troy High, tennis), Darius Feier (senior, Troy High, boys soccer), Steven Forman (senior, Troy High, tennis), Spencer Liu (senior, Troy High, tennis), Joseph Mason (senior, Troy High, boys soccer), Jessica Robinson (sophomore, Troy High, volleyball), Michael Song (junior, Troy High, tennis), Cole Valentine (senior, Athens, boys soccer) and Megan Worrel (senior, Troy High, cross country).

**Recognition 2.C and 2.D.** The Mission Moment features the Troy High School Auto Lab with David Easterbrook; the January 16 minutes elsewhere in this packet record that the Auto Lab had been highlighted on Channel 7 news and would have a booth at the International Auto Show at Cobo Hall. Principal Appreciation Month follows: throughout Michigan, February has traditionally been celebrated as Principal Appreciation Month in recognition of the work of building-level educational leaders, and the resolution recites that energetic and inspiring school leadership is essential if teachers, schools and districts are to ensure all Troy students are college and career ready, that K-12 principals act as the liaison between the school and the community it serves, and that Troy principals are dedicated, quality educational professionals — resolving that the Troy Board of Education officially recognizes February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy.

**Consent agenda.** A. Minutes of the December 5, 2017 Closed Session Meeting; B. Minutes of the January 9, 2018 Special Board of Education Meeting; C. Minutes of the January 9, 2018 Closed Session Meeting; D. Minutes of the January 9, 2018 Board of Education Workshop; E. Minutes of the January 16, 2018 Board of Education Organizational and Regular Meeting; F. Treasurer's Report – December 2017.

The December 5 and January 9 closed sessions were both held to discuss support-staff contract extensions — the Troy Education Secretarial Association (TESA) on December 5, the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA) on January 9 — with no other business conducted. The January 9 special meeting adopted resolution 18-001 going into closed session on the TESPA extension under Section 8(c) of the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, on a roll call with Mr. Miletti absent. The January 9 workshop covered public communication, an ALICE Crisis Response overview presented with Steve Brandimore from Safe-Ed and School Resource Officer John Julian of the Troy Police Department, and the 4th and 5th grade classroom furniture purchase.

**The January 16, 2018 organizational and regular meeting minutes.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; in addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff, Miletti and Schmidt were present and Mrs. Hammond was absent. All four high school student representatives attended, along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Griffor and Harris, and approximately 35 members of the audience. Every vote that evening carried 6-0 with Hammond absent.

Dr. Philippart served as acting chairperson (18-002) and appointed Judy Holmes temporary secretary. Mrs. Fleming nominated Mr. Schmidt for president (18-003), who was elected until December 31, 2018 on a 6-0 roll call. Mr. Miletti nominated Mr. Gottlieb for vice president (18-004), elected 6-0. Mr. Gottlieb nominated Mr. Hauff for secretary (18-005), elected 6-0. Resolution 18-006 appointed Rick L. West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer of the Troy Board of Education for January through December 2018.

Resolution 18-007 adopted the Fund Depositories and Investments resolution, naming Bank of America, Bank of New York, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, First Merit Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (the Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Monies may be withdrawn by checks bearing the facsimile signature of Treasurer Rick West, and in emergencies the handwritten signature of the Treasurer or of Superintendent Richard M. Machesky on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America; Troy Career Center accounts at PNC Bank are drawn on the handwritten signature of the Career Center Manager, Assistant Manager or Program Coordinators; the Comerica account for health care and dependent care flexible spending claims may be drawn by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc.; funds are invested according to Board Policy 5000.06; and the Treasurer is authorized to combine money from more than one fund for an investment authorized by subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code, with the maximum amount to be invested regulated by the school code. Gary N. Hauff certified the resolution as Secretary.

Resolution 18-008 continued the designation of Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk Albertson; LaPointe & Associates, P.C.; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. as legal counsel for the 2018 calendar year, with the superintendent authorized to consult additional counsel as needed on prior notification to the board. Resolution 18-009 continued the designation of the Superintendent as Deputy Secretary; 18-010 designated Judy Holmes, Secretary to the Superintendent of Schools, as the person for posting notices of meetings for 2018; and 18-011 adopted the schedule of meetings for the 2018 calendar year.

The consent agenda that night (18-012) approved the December 5, 2017 special meeting and workshop minutes, the December 19, 2017 meeting minutes, the Treasurer's Report for November 2017 and the corrected resolution from the 12/19/17 asbestos abatement. Mr. Schmidt mentioned that the corrected resolution for asbestos abatement was just an error naming the company that was awarded the bid — the name of the consulting firm had been inadvertently put in the initial resolution — and that the December 19 meeting minutes would also reflect the correction. Resolution 18-013 approved the extension of the TESPA, MEA/NEA contract through June 30, 2022. Resolution 18-014 approved the personnel recommendation, recorded in these minutes as new hires Rebecca Turner and Jill Flaherty. Resolution 18-015 approved the furniture purchase for 4th and 5th grade classrooms in the amount of $853,231.22 through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund; Dr. Philippart asked whether the district could donate the old desks as it had with the last furniture purchase, and Mr. Dziatczak said the district was looking into that.

Student representatives reported: Anjana Pisupati (IA-East) on enrollment applications, a HOSA competition at which over 70 medals were won, and the IASA Cultural Show; Nadia Shaouni (Troy College & Career High School) that 32 students began winter semester college classes at Oakland, Macomb and Washtenaw Community Colleges through Dual Enrollment; Tori Zarbaugh (Athens) on the ScreenAgers screening and Charity Week; and Hana Barre (Troy High) that Judge Hartig held court in school and that Activist Week funds would benefit elementary schools in Flint. Board members thanked Dr. Philippart for seven years as president — Mr. Miletti, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Gottlieb, Mrs. Fleming and Mr. Schmidt each spoke — and Dr. Machesky presented her a wood gavel and plaque; each Board member received a framed print of the district's four characteristics of World Class. The meeting adjourned at 8:01 p.m.

The totals are: Total General Fund $9,978,994.82, Total Special Revenue Funds $248,358.87, Total Other Funds $722,618.75, TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS $10,949,972.44 — a figure the check register itself confirms at TOTAL REPORT 10,949,972.44 — plus ACH debits $33,022.78, outgoing wire transfers $1,972,883.34 and P-Card purchases $179,070.01, less prior period void disbursements of $2,279.00, for TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD $13,132,669.57.
